Tertia virtus, quæ ornat mulierem magis
quàm smaragdus aut purpura, teste etiam
Cratete Thebano, est pudicitia, seu verecun-
dia, qua ornata fuit Susanna, Dan.13. Nam
multiplex gratia, vel, gratia super gratiam, in
quit noster Sapiens, est mulier pudica & fide-
lis .i. quum summus mulieris pudor (quo
cauet omnem in dictis & factis turpitudinê,
ex eaque hominum, in primisque mariti of-
fensionem) cum fidelitate (quę in rebus com-
missis creditisq; verfatur) coniungitur, nec
vlla re digne poteft rependi eius animi con-
tinentia: qua nimirum se continet non tan-
tùm à Venere, sed etiam à vino & multilo-
quio, discurfu, auaritia. Continentia enim
genus est ad quamplurimas suas species. Vt
autem pudicitia, quæ ex continenti animo
proficiscitur, decet mulierem: sic mores, fer-
mones & gestus obscoeni atq; turpes illam
dedecent.
Quarta est, honestas seu bonitas. Dicit e-
nim:

page.notes: The word after "quit" is printed as "quit" and may be a misprint for another word; kept as printed. "lua" in "quæ lua blandiloquentia" is a long s, read as "sua" and transcribed accordingly; the letter is not fully certain. "turpitudinê" has a doubtful final vowel mark. Line-end word "fide-lis" has no printed hyphen and is written whole. Short marks at the right edge and a stroke below the last line are not text and were left out.
